transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thanks so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, it's probably nothing major, but... I came in because my head just doesn't really stay on task anymore? 

Like, I'll be at work—I do building maintenance and cleaning—and I'll be doing inventory, or, um, trying to study for my supervisor certification, and I just keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk into the supply closet and totally forget what I even went in there for. 

I mean, I know everyone gets a little forgetful sometimes, right? It's probably just regular stress. But it's been happening enough that it's getting a bit frustrating, so I figured I should probably ask someone about it... if that makes sense?

Can you tell me if, when you're having trouble focusing, you also feel detached from yourself or like you're observing yourself from outside your body? Also, have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't feel like I'm outside my body or anything weird like that. I'm definitely still... me. I hope that's the right answer? 

But, um, as for feeling down... I guess maybe a little? I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for, but... most days, I just feel kind of... flat. Like there's this heavy feeling just kind of following me around. Even when I'm just pushing my cart down an empty hallway at work, or, you know, sitting at home with my family. I try really hard to act normal and be upbeat for them, I really do. I just... it's just been a bit harder to shake lately. Is that normal to feel sometimes?
Have you noticed that you feel tired or have a lack of energy most days, even when you haven't done anything particularly strenuous?

Um, tired? I mean, I guess I get a little tired sometimes, but who doesn't, right? My job keeps me on my feet a lot, so it's probably just that. I definitely don't want to sound lazy or anything. I always make sure I get my work done, and I try to help out around the house as much as I can. 

I wouldn't say I have a lack of energy, really. Just the normal amount of tired at the end of the day, I think. That's pretty standard, isn't it? I hope I'm answering this right, I just don't want to make a big deal out of nothing.
Can you tell me if you’ve had trouble thinking clearly or concentrating, even outside of work tasks—like when you're reading, watching TV, or making decisions?

Um, well... I guess I sort of mentioned the work stuff earlier, with the inventory and the supply closet. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I know your time is valuable. 

But, um, outside of work... I mean, I guess it happens a little bit? Like, I was trying to study for that supervisor certification at home the other night, and I just kept reading the same paragraph over and over again without it really sticking. And sometimes if I'm trying to figure out what to make for dinner, it just feels like my brain is... fuzzy? Like I can't quite piece the steps together as fast as I usually do. 

I don't think it's anything terrible, though. Probably just me being a little scattered, you know? I try really hard to stay on top of things for my family, I really do. I just... my head just doesn't stay on task like it used to. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope that makes sense.
Have you found that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with family, don’t bring you the same pleasure they used to?

Oh, no, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I still really love spending time with my family. They're everything to me, you know? I'd never want to give the impression that I don't care about them or that I don't enjoy being around them. I always try to make sure we have a good time together on my days off, even if I'm just watching the kids play. 

And as for hobbies... I mean, I don't have a ton of free time between my cleaning shifts and helping out at home, but when I do get a minute to myself, it's still nice. I still like doing the things I've always liked. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just really don't want you to think I'm, like, neglecting my family or being a bad dad or anything. I still care about all that stuff a lot, I promise. I'm doing okay in that department, right?
Can you tell me if your mood tends to stay the same, even when something good happens, like spending time with family or accomplishing something at work?

Um, well... I'd say I still get happy when good things happen. Like, if I finish a big cleaning project at work and the floors look really good, I definitely feel good about that. Or if we have a nice dinner at home, I enjoy it. 

I guess maybe... sometimes the good feeling doesn't last quite as long as it used to? But it's still there! I definitely still feel it. I try really hard to appreciate the good moments, you know? I'm always grateful for my family and my job. I'm not just walking around miserable all the time, I promise. I try to keep a positive attitude. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Have you noticed that even when something good happens, like finishing a task at work or spending time with your family, your overall mood still feels low or heavy for most of the day?

Um... I guess... well, I mean, I did just say I still get happy when good things happen, and I really do! I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or ungrateful. 

But... if I'm being completely honest... I guess there is this sort of... heavy feeling? Like, it's just kind of flat, and it follows me around most days. Even when I'm just pushing my cleaning cart down an empty hallway at work, or... or even when I'm sitting with my family and trying my best to act normal for them. The good moments happen, but that heavy feeling is just sort of... underneath it all? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a downer. I really try not to let it show, especially around the kids. I want to be a good dad and a good employee. Is... is it normal to feel like that sometimes? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Can you tell me if you've noticed a decrease in your ability to think clearly or concentrate, even when you're not particularly stressed or tired?

Um, well... I guess I have noticed a little bit of that, yeah. Actually, that's kind of the main reason I came in to see you. I really hope it's just stress or something, but... my head just doesn't seem to stay on task lately. 

Like, I'll be doing inventory for the cleaning supplies at work, or... or I'm trying to study for this supervisor certification I want to get, and I just keep reading the exact same line over and over. Or I'll walk all the way to the supply closet and completely forget what I went in there for. 

I mean, I know everyone gets forgetful sometimes, right? I'm sure it's probably nothing major, and I really try to double-check my work so I don't mess anything up for my boss. I want to make sure I'm still doing a good job. But it is a little frustrating. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen? I just don't want you to think I'm slacking off at work or anything like that.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or sad for most of the day, even when there’s no obvious reason for it?

Um... well, like I was saying earlier, I really try my best to keep a positive attitude. I don't want to be someone who just complains all the time, you know? I have a good life, a good job, and I'm really thankful for all of it. 

But... I guess... yeah, if I'm being totally honest, there is that feeling I mentioned. It's just this... heavy, flat kind of feeling. And it does seem to be there most days. Even when there's no real reason for it, like when I'm just pushing my cleaning cart down an empty hallway at work, or... or even when I'm sitting with my family and trying to act normal. It's just sort of... always there in the background. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything. I really do try to push through it and not let it bother anyone else. Is it okay that I feel like that sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed that activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with family, feel less satisfying or enjoyable than they used to, even if you still try to do them?

Um, actually... no, I don't think I've noticed that. I mean, I still really love spending time with my kids and my wife. And, you know, I still like watching the game on the weekends or just tinkering around the house. I really try to make the most of those moments, and I do still get a lot of joy out of them. 

I hope that's a good sign? I definitely don't want you to think I'm checking out on my family or not appreciating the good things I have. I really do still enjoy those activities... is it okay that I don't have that specific problem? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Even if you still enjoy time with family or your usual activities, have you noticed that you look forward to them less than before or that they take more effort to enjoy?

Um, no... I really don't think so. I still very much look forward to coming home after my shift. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I'm a little physically tired just from being on my feet all day, mopping and emptying the trash and everything, but... it doesn't take extra effort to actually enjoy being with them. I still get genuinely excited for, like, pizza night with the kids or just having some quiet time with my wife. It doesn't feel like a chore at all.

I hope that's okay? Like, I don't want to make it sound like I'm contradicting myself with that heavy feeling I told you about earlier. I just really value my family, and I wouldn't want you to think I'm taking them for granted or pulling away from them. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how things are.
Would you say that your mood stays low most of the day, nearly every day, even when nothing particularly bad is happening?

Um... yeah, I guess I'd have to say yes to that. Like I was saying a minute ago, it's just... it's this heavy, flat feeling that kind of follows me around most days. 

Even when nothing bad is happening at all. Like I said, I could just be pushing my cart down an empty hallway at work, just doing my normal routine, or... or even sitting right there with my family, trying my best to act normal and be present. And it's still just... there. Hanging over me.

I hope I'm not repeating myself too much? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. I really try not to let it show, and I definitely don't want to sound like I'm just feeling sorry for myself when I have so much to be grateful for. Is it helpful that I'm explaining it this way?
Would you say that your low mood has been present most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Um... well, two weeks? It's... it's actually been a lot longer than that, to be honest. 

I guess... well, it's been going on for about three years now. It kind of started back when the cleaning contractor I work for switched our schedules around. They moved us to these rotating evening and overnight shifts, mostly covering the larger commercial properties. 

I hope it's okay that I didn't mention how long it's been right away? I just... I didn't want to sound like I'm complaining about my job, because I'm really grateful to be working and providing for my family. A lot of guys would love to have the hours, you know? But yeah, that heavy feeling has kind of just been there since that schedule change happened, most days for the last three years. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Have you ever found that activities you used to really enjoy, like time with family or hobbies, don’t feel as rewarding or pleasurable as they used to, even if you still do them?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I know you asked something kind of like this a minute ago, and... and I really don't think I've lost the joy in those things. 

I still really love my hobbies—like, I like tinkering with old radios when I have a spare hour, and I still get a real kick out of getting one to work. And my family... they're my whole world. I still feel really happy when we're all together. It's just that heavy mood in the background, you know? But the actual things I love doing, they still feel just as good as they always did. 

I hope it's not frustrating that my answer is the same as before? I just want to be totally honest with you, and I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing interest in my kids or my wife. That's not the case at all. Am I explaining that okay?
Would you say that you take less pleasure or interest in most of the things you used to enjoy, even if you still do them?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, I know you just asked about this, and I hope I'm not being difficult by giving the same answer again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

I really do still enjoy the things I've always enjoyed. Like I said, fixing up those old radios still gives me a lot of satisfaction. And I still love spending time with my wife and kids. I haven't lost interest in any of that, I promise. It's just that low feeling that's always kind of there, but it doesn't stop me from enjoying my hobbies or my family. 

I'm sorry if it seems like I'm repeating myself. I just want to be sure I'm understanding your questions correctly. Is it okay that my answer is the same? I really want to be helpful and make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
